First, I know that iPods used to have FireWire, but later models switched to USB. So, the question is about a feature that keeps the USB interface powered even when the computer is off. I think this is a common feature on laptops to charge devices like phones or tablets without needing to keep the computer on.

I remember hearing terms like "PowerShare" or "Sleep & Charge" from Dell. Maybe one of these is the feature they're referring to. I should check if Dell actually uses these terms for this purpose.

I'll start by searching for "Dell PowerShare USB charging off Dell laptop" to see if that brings up relevant information. From the search results, it looks like Dell does have a feature called PowerShare that allows USB devices to charge even when the laptop is off. That makes sense.

From the documentation, it seems that PowerShare is the official term, and USB Wake Support might be an alternative name. Maybe the Planner confused the two terms.

So, the mistake here is that the Planner identified the feature as USB Wake Support instead of the correct term, PowerShare. This could be because the Planner didn't cross-reference the search results properly or didn't check the most recent Dell documentation.
